raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`tool_choice="none"` currently does two things: the prompt side withholds or soft-disables tools, and the response side turns the tool-call parser off (`_tool_call_parsing_active` returns False). Nothing stops the model from writing a call anyway, for example when the user explicitly insists on a tool. When it does, the call reaches the client as **raw template syntax in `message.content`**, because no parser consumes it.

Seen in production with Kimi K3 (`--tool-call-parser kimi_k3`). The user prompt was "query the weather, you must call get_weather", sent with `tools` and `tool_choice: "none"`. On engines that run this code path, 3 of 6 responses had content like:

```
<|open|>tools<|sep|><|open|>call tool="get_weather" index="1"<|sep|>...
```

The same failure class has come up before for other formats:
- #35393, closed: post-hoc stripping of unparsed K3 syntax.
- #40237, open: DeepSeek tool markup returned as content.
- #43006, merged: withholds DSV tools from the prompt under `none`, but cannot stop the model from emitting a call.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`:
- **`_tool_call_parsing_active`** is now true whenever tools and a parser are configured, including `tool_choice="none"`. The parser consumes the call's template syntax instead of leaking it.
- **New `_drop_tool_calls(request)`:** under `"none"`, parsed calls are discarded.
  - Non-streaming returns no `tool_calls`, and a `tool_calls` finish becomes `stop`.
  - Streaming emits no tool-call deltas, never sets `has_tool_calls`, and skips the leftover-argument flush.
- **Under `"none"` with tools present, `skip_special_tokens=False`, as under `"auto"`.** This keeps the markers the parser matches decodable. The glm47 full-assistant grammar case is left as is.
- **Unchanged:**
  - What goes into the prompt under `"none"` (`tools=None` on the jinja path, `tool_choice="none"` for the K3 encoder, DSV omission).
  - The K3 `TOOLS_CLOSE` stop stays scoped to active tools (`test_kimi_k3_tool_call_stop_is_scoped_to_active_tools` still passes).

A model that obeys `"none"` behaves exactly as before. A model that calls anyway now returns its text without the call, instead of the call's raw syntax.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output or kernel change. Response post-processing only.

Unit tests (CPU), in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`:
- `test_tool_choice_none_keeps_tool_call_parser_active`
- `test_kimi_k3_tool_choice_none_drops_call_non_stream`: `"none"` returns content `"I'll check the weather."`, no `tool_calls`, finish `stop`. The `"auto"` control returns 1 call with finish `tool_calls`.
- `test_kimi_k3_tool_choice_none_drops_call_stream`: the stream is fed in 7-character pieces. `"none"` streams only `"I'll check."`, with no tool-call deltas. The `"auto"` control still streams the call.

**Without the fix, the new tests fail with the production symptom:** `'<|open|>' unexpectedly found in "I'll check the weather.<|open|>tools<|sep|><|open|>call tool=\"get_weather\"…"`.

**Regressions:** `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/` and `test/registered/function_call/` were run on CPU with and without the patch.
- Same pre-existing environment failures on both (5 dsv4/dsv32/kimi-k3 encoding-detection tests need real model configs, and 3 modules failed to collect locally).
- With the patch: 510 passed, versus 507 without, the difference being the new tests. No new failures.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The extra cost only applies to `tool_choice="none"` requests with tools, which now run the same parser `"auto"` requests already run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Ran isort 7.0.0, ruff-format 0.15.1 and codespell 2.4.1 on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no user-facing flag changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

A stronger fix would be to stop the model from *starting* a call under `"none"`. For Kimi K3 that means a structural tag excluding `TOOLS_OPEN`, mirroring `get_kimik3_structural_tag(..., "required")`. It is left out here because grammar-constrained decoding under DSPARK with TP > 1 can currently deadlock (#41449), and DSPARK is a common K3 deployment recipe.

+    _K3_CALL = (
+        TOOLS_OPEN
+        + '<|open|>call tool="get_weather" index="1"<|sep|>'
+        + '<|open|>argument key="city" type="string"<|sep|>'
+        + "Beijing<|close|>argument<|sep|>"
+        + "<|close|>call<|sep|>"
+        + TOOLS_CLOSE
+    )
+
+    def _k3_ret(self, text):
+        return [
+            {
+                "text": text,
+                "meta_info": {
+                    "id": "chatcmpl-k3-none",
+                    "prompt_tokens": 12,
+                    "completion_tokens": 30,
+                    "cached_tokens": 0,
+                    "finish_reason": {"type": "stop", "matched": None},
+                    "weight_version": "default",
+                },
+            }
+        ]
+
+    def test_tool_choice_none_keeps_tool_call_parser_active(self):
+        """A call the model writes anyway under tool_choice="none" must still be
+        consumed by the parser, or its template syntax reaches content."""
+        self.chat.tool_call_parser = "kimi_k3"
+        for tool_choice in ("none", "auto"):
+            with self.subTest(tool_choice=tool_choice):
+                request = ChatCompletionRequest(
+                    model="x",
+                    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Beijing?"}],
+                    tools=[self._K3_WEATHER_TOOL],
+                    tool_choice=tool_choice,
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(self.chat._tool_call_parsing_active(request))
+        no_tools = ChatCompletionRequest(
+            model="x", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(self.chat._tool_call_parsing_active(no_tools))
+
+    def test_kimi_k3_tool_choice_none_drops_call_non_stream(self):
+        self.chat.chat_encoding_spec = "kimi_k3"
+        self.chat.tool_call_parser = "kimi_k3"
+        text = "I'll check the weather." + self._K3_CALL
+        for tool_choice, expect_calls in (("none", False), ("auto", True)):
+            with self.subTest(tool_choice=tool_choice):
+                request = ChatCompletionRequest(
+                    model="x",
+                    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Beijing?"}],
+                    tools=[self._K3_WEATHER_TOOL],
+                    tool_choice=tool_choice,
+                )
+                response = self.chat._build_chat_response(
+                    request, self._k3_ret(text), created=123
+                )
+                choice = response.choices[0]
+                content = choice.message.content or ""
+                self.assertNotIn("<|open|>", content)
+                self.assertNotIn("<|close|>", content)
+                if expect_calls:
+                    self.assertEqual(len(choice.message.tool_calls), 1)
+                    self.assertEqual(choice.finish_reason, "tool_calls")
+                else:
+                    self.assertFalse(choice.message.tool_calls)
+                    self.assertEqual(choice.finish_reason, "stop")
+                    self.assertEqual(content, "I'll check the weather.")
+
+    def test_kimi_k3_tool_choice_none_drops_call_stream(self):
+        self.chat.chat_encoding_spec = "kimi_k3"
+        self.chat.tool_call_parser = "kimi_k3"
+        text = "I'll check." + self._K3_CALL
+        pieces = [text[i : i + 7] for i in range(0, len(text), 7)]
+
+        async def run(tool_choice):
+            request = ChatCompletionRequest(
+                model="x",
+                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Beijing?"}],
+                tools=[self._K3_WEATHER_TOOL],
+                tool_choice=tool_choice,
+                stream=True,
+            )
+            parser_dict, has_tool_calls, lines = {}, {}, []
+            for piece in pieces:
+                async for line in self.chat._process_tool_call_stream(
+                    index=0,
+                    delta=piece,
+                    parser_dict=parser_dict,
+                    content={"meta_info": {"id": "chatcmpl-k3-none"}},
+                    request=request,
+                    has_tool_calls=has_tool_calls,
+                    created=123,
+                ):
+                    if line:
+                        lines.append(line)
+            return lines, has_tool_calls
+
+        loop = get_or_create_event_loop()
+        for tool_choice, expect_calls in (("none", False), ("auto", True)):
+            with self.subTest(tool_choice=tool_choice):
+                lines, has_tool_calls = loop.run_until_complete(run(tool_choice))
+                deltas = [
+                    json.loads(line[len("data: ") :])["choices"][0]["delta"]
+                    for line in lines
+                ]
+                streamed = "".join(d.get("content") or "" for d in deltas)
+                self.assertNotIn("<|open|>", streamed)
+                self.assertEqual(streamed, "I'll check.")
+                self.assertEqual(any(d.get("tool_calls") for d in deltas), expect_calls)
+                self.assertEqual(bool(has_tool_calls.get(0)), expect_calls)
+
     def test_dsv_tool_choice_none_omits_tools_from_prompt(self):
         self.template_manager.chat_template_name = None
         self.template_manager.jinja_template_content_format = "string"
